118	pub const fn priv_index(id: PrivId) -> Option<usize> {
119	    let n = id.as_usize();
120	    if n >= NR_SYS_PROCS { None } else { Some(n) }

--- md ---
CLAUDE.md:169:- Minimal signals (slice 4.5): the kernel half is `system/do_sig.rs` — `SYS_KILL` → `cause_sig` sets a bit in `Proc::sig_pending` (u32 bitmap; zeroed on slot free and again on fork's child populate) plus `RTS_SIGNALED|RTS_SIG_PENDING`, then wakes PM with `ipc::notify::deliver_ksig` (kernel-originated `NOTIFY` from `SYSTEM`, no `ipc_to` check — the `deliver_alarm` pattern; `do_kill`'s deferred-notify write is why `kernel_call_dispatch` takes `&mut [Priv]`). Drain contract (amended in 4.6a): `SYS_GETKSIG` hands off the bitmap (its scan gates on `sig_pending != 0`, not the RTS bit alone, so a handed-off proc isn't re-returned) and PM disposes of every returned endpoint — `SYS_ENDKSIG` for survivors, `SYS_EXIT` (with **no** ENDKSIG after) for terminations, since 4.6's full exit zeroes signal state and frees the slot so a post-exit acknowledge just bounces off `okendpt` with `EDEADSRCDST`. `SYS_EXIT` is a **full teardown** as of 4.6a (`do_exit.rs`): stop + `caller_q` unlink as before, then `unblock_dependents` (every proc blocked SENDING-to/RECEIVING-from the dead endpoint resumes with `EDEADSRCDST` patched into its parked `x0`; dedicated-priv `notify_pending` bits purged, shared `USER_PRIV_ID` deliberately skipped), leaf frames freed via `addrspace::walk_leaves` + `flush_tlb_asid` + `AddrSpace::destroy` + `asid::free_asid` (ASIDs recycle through a free-list now), and `free_slot` (endpoint `bump_generation` — wraps to 1, never 0 — all per-proc state zeroed, `RTS_SLOT_FREE` stored). Every user-supplied-endpoint resolution goes through `table::okendpt` (stored-endpoint + not-free check → `EDEADSRCDST` on stale generations): `mini_send`/`mini_notify` dst, `mini_receive`'s non-ANY filter, and the target-taking kernel calls via `system::resolve_target` (`SELF` short-circuits first; `do_exit` rejects SELF and caller-named-self outright — tearing down the active TTBR0 mid-call is the hazard). `SYS_PRIVCTL` has one subcode, `PRIVCTL_SET_USER`: requires the target frozen on `RTS_NO_PRIV` (the freeze doubles as the authorization gate; EPERM on a live target) and points it at the shared `table::USER_PRIV_ID` = 20 (`USR_T`, `ipc_to` = {PM}, empty `k_call_mask`, `sig_mgr` = PM; `populate_user_priv` opens the reverse PM(priv 5)→20 `ipc_to` edge at boot). Frozen-stub pattern: `build_stub(nr, None, .., frozen: true)` = full AS built (ttbr0/asid set, satisfying `schedule_next`'s asserts), no priv, not enqueued — `PRIVCTL_SET_USER` releases it. PM's request range is `PM_RQ_BASE = 0x700` (the gap below VM `0xC00` — SCHED's `0xF00` was the last block under `NOTIFY_MESSAGE`); `PM_GETPID` replies `m_type` = pid (MINIX result-is-pid, errors negative — PM's own pid 0 is indistinguishable from `OK` by design) with ppid in payload `0..4`. # tests/qemu-boot.expected -- required substrings for a healthy QEMU boot log.
# One literal substring per line; blank lines and '#' comments are ignored.
# Checked by tools/check-boot-log.sh via `grep -aF` (the log interleaves raw
# single-char tick bytes, so it must be forced to text). Substrings stop just
# before the first run-variable field (ttbr0_pa / child_e / entry / freed / at);
# nr= values are fixed boot-table slots (kernel-shared/src/com.rs).

# Kernel banner (kernel/src/main.rs)
minix.rs booting on aarch64

# Address-space bring-up: 8 servers + init (arch/aarch64/userland.rs). The tty
# line is new in slice 5.3 -- the first user-space *driver*, packed between ds and
# vfs so the console is in its receive loop before its first client.
[as] vm nr=7 ttbr0_pa=
[as] ds nr=5 ttbr0_pa=
[as] tty nr=4 ttbr0_pa=
[as] vfs nr=1 ttbr0_pa=
[as] sched nr=9 ttbr0_pa=
[as] rs nr=2 ttbr0_pa=
[as] pm nr=0 ttbr0_pa=
[as] init nr=10 ttbr0_pa=

# ...plus the 4 boot stubs (12 [as] lines total)
[as] stub A nr=11 ttbr0_pa=
[as] stub B nr=12 ttbr0_pa=
[as] stub C nr=13 ttbr0_pa=
[as] stub D nr=14 ttbr0_pa=

# init's fork/exec/wait cycle (head-carved kernel traces; slot 15 is the
# fork-pool base, recycled every cycle; exec renames the child to "worker")
[ksys SYS_FORK] parent=i nr=10 child_nr=15
[ksys SYS_EXEC] target=15 name=worker entry=
[ksys SYS_EXIT] target=w nr=15 freed=

# Stub D's designed SIGSEGV chain: page fault -> VM -> SYS_KILL sig=11 -> PM
# tears the stub down with SYS_EXIT
[pf] proc=D far=
[ksys SYS_KILL] target=D nr=14 sig=11 -> pm
[ksys SYS_EXIT] target=D nr=14 freed=

# RS's periodic kernel alarm: assert only the FIRST fire (always inside the
# head carve-out) -- timing-robust under slow CI TCG, unlike a fire count
[alarm 1] owner=r nr=2 at=

# Slice 5.1: stub A's one-shot bad-pointer probes. Each returns EFAULT instead
# of taking an EL1 data abort (which the forbidden list catches as a panic).
# Between them they cover every arm of the copy engine: probe 1 is a fully
# unmapped page, probe 2 straddles A's stack page into the unmapped one above
# it, probe 3 fails in the deferred MF_DELIVERMSG flush and lands EFAULT in A's
# parked x0, and probe 4 names A's *mapped but read-only* code page -- the only
# check on that path is the copy engine's own Prot::writable test, since the
# kernel writes through the HHDM alias where EL0 permission bits do not apply.
# call=1 is SEND; nr=11 is stub A. These lines are unsampled, so unlike
# `[ipc N]` they cannot drift with IPC ordering.
[efault] proc=A nr=11 call=1 va=0x900000
[efault] proc=A nr=11 call=1 va=0x800ff8
[efault deliver] proc=A nr=11 va=0x900000
[efault deliver] proc=A nr=11 va=0x400000

# Slice 5.1: SYS_DIAGCTL is real -- every SEF server announces itself from EL0
# through the kernel debug channel. The name prefix comes from the kernel's own
# proc slot, not the payload, so these lines cannot be spoofed. Assert two of
# the six: vm is the first server packed in the MXBI archive, pm the last, so
# together they bracket the whole roster.
[diag vm] sef ready
[diag pm] sef ready

# Slice 5.2: the grant engine, end to end. VFS direct-grants PM a 64-byte
# read-only buffer and hands the id over in a PM_GRANT_TEST message; PM reads it
# through the grant, then reads the *same* bytes again with the ungranted
# SYS_COPY and compares. `match=1` is the whole point — it proves the grant path
# moved the right bytes, not merely some bytes. Registration is per-granter, so
# both VFS (proc=1) and PM (proc=0) appear; assert VFS's, which is the one the
# demo's grant is served from.
[ksys SYS_SETGRANT] proc=1 entries=
[ksys SYS_SAFECOPY] granter=
[ksys SYS_COPY] src=
[diag pm] grant.test ok
[diag pm] copy ok match=1

# ...and the magic (third-party) arm: PM grants *itself* access to init's text
# page and safecopies out of init's address space, a process that granted
# nothing. Only the length is asserted — the bytes are init's instruction
# encodings and change whenever init is rebuilt. Without this line the magic
# path would be dead code until slice 5.5.
[diag pm] magic ok

# Slice 5.2: the copies that must be REFUSED. Seven safecopies, each valid in
# every respect but one. Five are EPERM from `verify_grant` — wrong grantee,
# wrong access, stale sequence, out-of-range index, past the end of the granted
# range — and two are EFAULT from the copy engine itself: a granter claiming
# CPF_WRITE over its own read-only .rodata (only `Prot::writable` stands between
# that lie and a corrupted page, since the kernel copies through the HHDM alias)
# and a well-formed grant over an unmapped page. Remove any one of those checks
# and that copy succeeds, so this line turns into `grant.deny FAIL <which>` and
# the marker disappears. (The `CPF_INDIRECT` and magic-`SYS_PROC` arms are not
# probed; see `grant_denials` in servers/pm for why neither is reachable yet.)
[diag pm] grant.deny ok

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Slice 5.3: the TTY console driver and the CDEV band.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The driver announces itself on the kernel debug channel, exactly like the six SEF

[diag tty] sef ready

# to Phase 6, so this is a bring-up step like the stack page). va/pa are fixed

# non-writable Prot, and TTY's first register store takes an EL0 data abort -- which
# the forbidden list catches.

# actually seen (a guard that skipped every leaf would give freed=0 devs=0).
# Unconditional, so the --no-default-features boot covers it too.
[devmap] selftest ok freed=0 devs=1

# ([as] / [ipc] / [ksys] / [diag] / [pf] / [devmap]); this one was composed at EL0
# and reached the wire through a user-space store to a device register.

# allocator, and it is the difference between "write returns a count" and "write

**Proof:** init's banner reaches serial through VFS→TTY; `[ipc]` head
traces show init→VFS SENDREC + VFS→TTY CDEV round-trip.

**As built** (differences from the sketch above, recorded so later slices do
not rediscover them):

- **init reports through the path it tests, and that forced a fourth marker.**
  init holds the shared USER privilege — no kernel calls, so no `SYS_DIAGCTL` and
  no debug channel of any kind. `write()` is the only thing it can say anything
  with, which is a nice property (a regression takes the evidence with it) but
  means every assertion has to be phrased as console text. The banner and the
  `vfs.deny ok n=3` summary were in the plan; the **`vfs.long ok match=1`** line
  was not, and it turned out to be load-bearing. Without it *nothing* checked a
  successful write's return value — init ignores it — so "reply `OK` instead of
  the byte count", which the plan listed as a mutation expected to produce a
  `FAIL`, moved no marker at all. The tail marker `vfs-loop-end` does not cover
  it either: a `write()` that moves every byte and then reports `OK` prints the
  tail and is still broken, in exactly the way a caller looping on the result
  would hit forever. Two markers, two independent halves of one contract.
- **The short-write loop clamps rather than trusts the driver.** `off +=
  n` would walk past the buffer if a driver ever reported more than it was asked
  for, and over-report the write; `off.saturating_add(n).min(len)` cannot. TTY is
  trusted today, but the loop is the shape every future block/FS driver client
  copies. A driver reporting `0` breaks the loop rather than re-sending forever —
  a server that spins is worse than a short write.
- **An error after partial progress reports the progress**, not the error (POSIX).
  The bytes really did go out, and telling the caller otherwise makes it send them
  twice. The error resurfaces on the next write, where it is still true.
- **`user_range_ok` is defence in depth, and the mutation table says so.** Removing
  it changes no marker: the kernel's copy engine walks the caller's page tables and
  answers `EFAULT` regardless (D5), which is the load-bearing gate. It stays because
  rejecting a malformed buffer before issuing a grant is cheaper and more legible
  than discovering it two hops away — but nothing should mistake it for the check
  that makes the path safe.
- **The fd table is an immutable `static`, so VFS still carries zero `unsafe`.**
  Nothing opens or closes in 5.4, so the table is fully determined at compile time
  and needs no interior mutability. Slice 5.8's `open` flips storage to the
  `UnsafeCell<[FdRow; N]>` + `unsafe impl Sync` newtype `vm/region.rs` and
  `ds/registry.rs` already use; `resolve_in` takes the rows as a borrowed slice
  precisely so it survives that switch untouched. Sized from `NR_SERVED_PROCS`,
  the shared ceiling, with the same `const _` guard PM/VM/SCHED carry.
- **`NR_FDS = 4`, not 3.** The fourth slot exists so "past the end of the row" and
  "in range but not open" are distinguishable cases in a test — and the `bad-fd`
  boot probe uses descriptor 3 for exactly that reason, since a descriptor that is
  merely out of bounds would be rejected by arithmetic rather than by the table.
- **`resolve` returns `Fd`, not a minor**, and `do_write` matches on it. The
  `Ok(Fd::Unused)` arm is unreachable today (`resolve` maps a closed descriptor to
  `EBADF` itself) and is kept so 5.8's regular-file variant lands as a compile
  error to be routed rather than a silent fallthrough.
- **VFS resolves TTY once, in `main`.** `tty_endpoint` moved out of `tty_demo`; a
  DS round-trip per `write()` would be a lookup per write for an endpoint that
  cannot change. The 5.3 demos are kept in full — they are the regression battery
  for the three contracts the real path does not reach (the *direct* grant form,
  the *visible* short write, and the two `CDEV_WRITE` refusals a well-formed
  `write()` never provokes).
- **The C header emits `VFS_WRITE` but not its payload offsets.** Same deferral
  the CDEV band uses, for a nearer reason: slice 5.6's `write()` wrapper is
  precisely the C that will need `VFS_FD_OFF`/`VFS_LEN_OFF`/`VFS_BUF_OFF`, so the
  test asserting their absence is what makes emitting them a deliberate act in that
  slice rather than something that drifted in early and froze un-reviewed at the
  ABI freeze.
- **The USER `ipc_to` widening is a list, not a second lookup.** `populate_user_priv`
  now loops over `USER_IPC_TO = [PM, VFS]`, resolving every server's priv slot in one
  read-only pass before taking any `&mut Priv` — the borrow discipline the existing
  `// SAFETY:` comments already justified, now with two servers instead of one.
  Every entry costs a *pair* of bits: `init_boot_image` fills a boot server's bitmap
  only over `[0, n_active)`, and `USER_PRIV_ID` is 20, so each reverse reply edge
  must be opened explicitly. The mutation table below shows the two directions
  failing in visibly different ways, which is worth knowing when adding a third
  server (5.8's MFS will not need one — a user process talks to VFS, not to MFS).

**Honest gaps:**

- **The confused-deputy rule is proved by construction, not by probe.** There is no
  `who_from` field in `VFS_WRITE`, so no boot marker can demonstrate a client
  failing to spoof one — the same shape as 5.2's unprobeable magic-`SYS_PROC` gate
  and 5.3's absent granter field. The mutation below (add such a field) is the only
  evidence, and it is evidence about a build that does not exist.
- **Only one process ever writes.** init is the sole `VFS_WRITE` client, so the fd
  table's per-process rows are exercised at exactly one index at runtime; the host
  tests sweep the whole `NR_SERVED_PROCS` range instead. Nothing yet writes from a
  forked child, which is what would prove the inherited-descriptor story end to end.

**Mutation tests run** (each applied, observed, reverted):

| Mutation | Observed |
|---|---|
| Read the grant's owner from a payload field instead of `m_source` | all four init markers vanish — the grant names the wrong owner, so TTY's safecopy is refused and every write fails. TTY itself stays online, so the failure is localized to the new path |
| Drop VFS's short-write loop (single `CDEV_WRITE`) | `vfs-loop-end` **and** `vfs.long ok match=1` vanish (`vfs.long FAIL` printed); banner and `vfs.deny ok n=3` survive — the two markers really are independent halves |
| Make `resolve_in` accept any descriptor | `vfs.deny ok n=3` → `vfs.deny FAIL bad-fd` (the write to descriptor 3 succeeded) |
| Drop the `ipc_to += VFS` bit in `populate_user_priv` | all four init markers vanish — init's SENDREC is refused before VFS ever sees it |
| Drop the reverse VFS → USER `ipc_to` bit | the banner **still prints** (the request was delivered and served; only the *reply* is refused), then init hangs in that SENDREC forever — so the other three init markers and all three `SYS_FORK`/`SYS_EXEC`/`SYS_EXIT` cycle markers vanish. 6 missing |
| Reply `OK` instead of the byte count from `do_write` | `vfs.long FAIL`, and `vfs.deny FAIL bad-buf` — the `EFAULT` probe reads as success. `bad-fd`/`no-such` still pass, since both return before the mutated line |
| Drop the `user_range_ok` pre-check | **nothing moves** — all 51 markers still pass. Confirms it is defence in depth and the kernel's page-table walk is the load-bearing `EFAULT` gate |

## Request-number ranges

Every server's request numbers occupy a distinct band below `NOTIFY_MESSAGE`, so
a message type unambiguously identifies both its server and its meaning
(`kernel-shared/src/callnr.rs`, const-asserted disjoint). The bands are listed —
and rendered into the generated C header — in ascending numeric order, so
`0x800` / `0x900` / `0xA00` are reserved for the three bands Phase 5 still owes:
VFS, BDEV, and MFS.

| Base | Value | Server / purpose |
|------|-------|------------------|
| `PM_RQ_BASE`    | `0x700` | PM: `PM_GETPID` / `FORK` / `EXIT` / `WAIT` / `EXEC` |
| `CDEV_RQ_BASE`  | `0xB00` | Character drivers: `CDEV_WRITE` (TTY) |
| `VM_RQ_BASE`    | `0xC00` | VM: `VM_PAGEFAULT` / `BRK` / `MMAP` / `MUNMAP` / `FORK` |
| `SEF_RQ_BASE`   | `0xD00` | SEF control messages (ping / signal / init) |
| `DS_RQ_BASE`    | `0xE00` | DS: `DS_PUBLISH` / `RETRIEVE` / `CHECK` |
| `SCHED_RQ_BASE` | `0xF00` | SCHED: `SCHEDULING_NO_QUANTUM` / `START` / `STOP` / `SET_NICE` |

## SEF: the server runtime
## VFS: skeletal

**VFS** (`servers/vfs/`) boots through SEF and publishes to DS, but does **no**
file operations yet: its receive loop drops any application message it gets. File
descriptors, the PM↔VFS work protocol, and real filesystem I/O require the
Phase-5 musl fork and file-system servers.

It is, however, already the system's first *grant* client and its first *console*
client. At startup it direct-grants a read-only buffer to PM (proving the
cross-address-space copy engine, slice 5.2), then looks TTY up in DS and drives
`CDEV_WRITE` — a real write, a deliberately over-long write that must come back
short, and two requests that must be refused (slice 5.3). Both are demo wiring in
the sense that no client asks for them yet, but neither is throwaway: slice 5.4
puts VFS's fd 1 and 2 on the same `CDEV_WRITE` path, using a magic grant over the
*caller's* buffer so the data still moves in a single copy.

## init: PID 1

**init** (`userland/init/`) is the first real user process and the live exercise
for everything above. Unlike the demo stubs it replaced, it is a genuine boot
module: `build.rs` packs it into the MXBI archive with its true proc number
(`INIT_PROC_NR = 10`), and the ordinary boot loop loads it and makes it runnable —
PM does not hand-release it. It runs at user grade, sharing the `USER_PRIV_ID`
privilege (SENDREC to PM only, no kernel calls) with every forked child.

init is a plain `minix-ipc` program — no SEF, because it is not a server. Its
whole body is a respawn loop: `PM_FORK`; the child (`m_type == 0`) issues
`PM_EXEC` to become the `worker` binary, which runs a few `PM_GETPID` round-trips
and exits; the parent (`m_type > 0`) issues `PM_WAIT` to reap the zombie, then
loops. Each cycle recycles a fork-pool slot with a fresh endpoint generation —
observable in the boot trace as repeating `SYS_FORK` → `SYS_EXEC name=worker` →
`SYS_EXIT` triples, the proof that fork, exec, teardown, and reap all compose.

The demo stubs A–D remain installed alongside init as a live regression battery:
A↔B exercise the raw SEND/RECEIVE/SENDREC primitives, C exercises the
kernel→SCHED quantum-delegation round-trip, and D exercises the page-fault→VM path
and the out-of-region SIGSEGV kill — coverage that init and worker, which only

## VFS: the write path

**VFS** (`servers/vfs/`) turns a small integer into something you can write to.
That is the whole of its job in Phase 5 so far, and since slice 5.4 it does it for
real: an ordinary user process can `write(1, buf, len)` and see bytes on the
console. Mount points, `open`, and reads arrive with the MFS server in slice 5.8.

### One request, one copy

```text
user ──VFS_WRITE{fd,buf,len}──► VFS ──CDEV_WRITE{minor,gid,len,off}──► TTY
                                 │                                      │
                                 └── magic grant: caller's buf ──────────┘
                                         (kernel copies, once)
```

VFS resolves the descriptor, issues a **magic** (third-party) grant naming the
*caller's* buffer with the driver as grantee, and forwards the grant id. TTY then
safecopies straight out of the caller's address space. The bytes never pass
through VFS: there is exactly one copy, from the process that wrote them to the
driver that transmits them. This is the first consumer of the magic grant form on
a real data path, and the rail slice 5.6's musl `write()` lands on.

Three properties hold that path together:

- **The grant's owner is the kernel-stamped `m_source`.** VFS holds `SYS_PROC`,
  which is what makes a magic grant legal for it at all — so a caller-supplied
  owner field would let any VFS client aim a privileged cross-address-space copy
  at a third party's memory. `VFS_WRITE` has no such field, and must never gain
  one. It is the same anti-confused-deputy rule that keeps a granter out of the
  `CDEV_WRITE` payload, applied to the granting side.
- **VFS absorbs short writes.** A character driver may move fewer bytes than asked
  (`CDEV_MAX_IO`, its staging limit); POSIX `write()` is not allowed to expose
  that, so VFS re-sends with `offset` advanced until the buffer is out and reports
  the total. One grant covers the whole buffer — only the offset moves. An error
  after partial progress reports the *progress*, since those bytes really did go
  out.
- **Every request gets a reply**, including an unknown one (`ENOSYS`). VFS's
  clients are all inside a SENDREC, so a dropped message blocks the caller forever.

### The descriptor table

`servers/vfs/src/fd.rs` holds one row of descriptors per process, indexed by
kernel proc number and sized from the shared `NR_SERVED_PROCS` ceiling that PM's
`mproc` and VM's `ClientRegions` also derive from. Nothing opens or closes yet, so
every row is identical — fds 0, 1, and 2 name the console, everything else is
`EBADF` — which is POSIX's inheritance convention and is what lets init write
before any filesystem exists. Because nothing mutates, the storage is an ordinary
immutable `static` and VFS carries no `unsafe`; slice 5.8's `open` flips it to the
`UnsafeCell` newtype that VM's region table already uses.

VFS also remains the system's first *grant* client and first *console* client:
its startup still direct-grants a read-only buffer to PM (slice 5.2) and drives
`CDEV_WRITE` by hand (slice 5.3). Those are kept deliberately, as the regression
battery for three contracts the real write path never reaches — the direct-grant
form, a *visible* short write, and the two `CDEV_WRITE` refusals a well-formed
`write()` cannot provoke.

Slice 5.4 is implemented and verified. All gates green:

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `fmt --check`, `clippy --workspace --all-targets` | clean |
| `clippy -p minixrs-kernel` (default + `--no-default-features`) | clean |
| `cargo test` (kernel-shared / vfs / gen-c-headers) | 175 pass |
| C ABI gate (regenerate + hermetic `clang -fsyntax-only`) | OK, nothing written into the tree |
| QEMU boot + `check-boot-log.sh` | **51/51 markers** (was 47) |
| Stub-free boot | all four new markers present |

**What landed:** `VFS_RQ_BASE = 0x800` / `VFS_WRITE` with the neighbours' bounds retargeted (PM→VFS→CDEV); the band inserted 7th in the C generator with both new ordering asserts; `servers/vfs/src/fd.rs` (new, host-tested, 8 tests); `do_write` + `write_all` in VFS; `USER_IPC_TO = [PM, VFS]` in `populate_user_priv`; init's writes; markers and docs.

**Two deviations from the plan, both deliberate:**

1. **Added a fourth marker, `vfs.long ok match=1`.** The plan's mutation table expected "reply `OK` instead of the byte count" to produce a `FAIL` — but nothing checked a *successful* write's return value (init ignored it), so that mutation moved no marker at all. `vfs-loop-end` doesn't cover it either: a write that moves every byte and returns `OK` still prints the tail. init now checks the long write's count against what it asked for, which makes the plan's own proof requirement achievable and gives mutation 2 a second signal.

2. **`write_all` clamps with `.min(len)`** rather than a bare `off += n`, so an over-reporting driver can't walk past the buffer and over-report the write.

**Mutation tests** — all seven run against the final 51-marker baseline, each applied/observed/reverted from scratchpad copies; `diff -q` confirms all four touched files byte-identical and `grep -rn MUTATION` finds only CLAUDE.md's own instruction. Two results differ from the plan's predictions and are recorded as such:

- **Dropping the reverse VFS→USER `ipc_to` bit** leaves the banner *printing* — the request is delivered and served, only the reply is refused — then init hangs mid-SENDREC, taking the other three init markers plus all three fork/exec/exit markers (6 missing, not "all three init lines").
- **Mutation 6** moves two markers (`vfs.long FAIL` **and** `vfs.deny FAIL bad-buf`); `bad-fd`/`no-such` still pass because both return before the mutated line.
- **Dropping `user_range_ok` moves nothing** — 51/51 still pass, confirming it's defence in depth and the kernel's page-table walk is the load-bearing `EFAULT` gate. Recorded in the plan doc's mutation table.

One honest gap worth flagging: the confused-deputy rule is proved only by construction — there's no `who_from` field, so no boot marker can show a client failing to spoof one. Same shape as 5.2's unprobeable magic-`SYS_PROC` gate; it's written up in the doc's "Honest gaps".

I have **not** committed — your workflow says to surface changes for review first, and the pre-PR checklist wants your sign-off before the PR. The branch is `feature/slice-5.4-vfs-write`; 11 files modified plus `servers/vfs/src/fd.rs` untracked.

attachment.snippet:
1	# Servers
2	
3	minix.rs keeps the microkernel tiny — IPC, scheduling, memory protection, and a
4	small set of privileged kernel calls — and runs every operating-system *service*
5	as an ordinary user-space process, exactly as MINIX 3 does. These **servers**
6	talk to each other and to the kernel only through message passing. A server never
7	shares memory with a client; it acts on a request, replies, and the kernel
8	enforces who may talk to whom via per-process privilege bitmaps.
9	
10	This chapter describes the servers as they stand at the end of Phase 4: a common
11	runtime (SEF), a name registry (DS), a user-space scheduler (SCHED), a monitor
12	(RS), the process manager (PM), a still-skeletal file-system switch (VFS), and
13	`init` (PID 1) — the first real user process, which drives the whole
14	fork/exec/wait lifecycle through PM.
15	
16	## Where servers live
17	
18	Servers are freestanding `#![no_std]` / `#![no_main]` ELF binaries linked with
19	their own `user.ld` (page-aligned segments based at `0x0010_0000`) and branded
20	with the minixrs ELF identity note, which the kernel requires of every image it
21	loads. The kernel's `build.rs` compiles each for the `aarch64-unknown-minixrs`
22	target and concatenates them into a single **MXBI archive** embedded in the
23	kernel image; the boot loader
24	(`kernel/src/arch/aarch64/userland.rs`) walks the archive and loads each module
25	into the proc slot named by its record. Each server gets its own per-process
26	TTBR0, so they all share the same low load base with no collision.
27	
28	A server has no `println`. Its behaviour is observed through kernel-side traces
29	(`[ipc]`, `[ksys]`, `[pf]`, `[alarm]`), and since slice 5.1 it can also emit a
30	line itself through the kernel debug channel — `server-rt`'s `diag_print` /
31	`diag_fmt` issue a `SYS_DIAGCTL` carrying the text inline, which the kernel prints
32	prefixed with the caller's own name (`[diag vfs] …`). That is deliberately a
33	*debug* channel, not stdio: it exists to keep working while stdio itself is under
34	construction. Real console output arrives via the TTY driver (see
35	[Drivers](../drivers/overview.md)) — slice 5.3 put the first EL0-composed text on
36	the serial line, and slice 5.4 puts a process's fd 1 and 2 on top of it.
37	
38	## Request-number ranges
39	
40	Every server's request numbers occupy a distinct band below `NOTIFY_MESSAGE`, so
41	a message type unambiguously identifies both its server and its meaning
42	(`kernel-shared/src/callnr.rs`, const-asserted disjoint). The bands are listed —
43	and rendered into the generated C header — in ascending numeric order. VFS took
44	`0x800` in slice 5.4; `0x900` and `0xA00` stay reserved for the two bands Phase 5
45	still owes, BDEV and MFS.
46	
47	| Base | Value | Server / purpose |
48	|------|-------|------------------|
49	| `PM_RQ_BASE`    | `0x700` | PM: `PM_GETPID` / `FORK` / `EXIT` / `WAIT` / `EXEC` |
50	| `VFS_RQ_BASE`   | `0x800` | VFS: `VFS_WRITE` |
51	| `CDEV_RQ_BASE`  | `0xB00` | Character drivers: `CDEV_WRITE` (TTY) |
52	| `VM_RQ_BASE`    | `0xC00` | VM: `VM_PAGEFAULT` / `BRK` / `MMAP` / `MUNMAP` / `FORK` |
53	| `SEF_RQ_BASE`   | `0xD00` | SEF control messages (ping / signal / init) |
54	| `DS_RQ_BASE`    | `0xE00` | DS: `DS_PUBLISH` / `RETRIEVE` / `CHECK` |
55	| `SCHED_RQ_BASE` | `0xF00` | SCHED: `SCHEDULING_NO_QUANTUM` / `START` / `STOP` / `SET_NICE` |
56	
57	## SEF: the server runtime
58	
59	`server-rt` is minix.rs's small equivalent of MINIX 3's SEF (System Event
60	Framework). A server calls `sef_startup(SefConfig { init_fresh, signal_handler })`,
61	which learns the server's own endpoint and name from the kernel via
62	`SYS_GETINFO(GET_WHOAMI)`, runs the optional `init_fresh` callback, and returns a
63	`Sef` handle. The main loop is then `loop { if sef.receive(&mut msg) != 0 { continue } match msg.m_type { … } }`:
64	`sef.receive` wraps `ipc_receive(ANY, …)` and transparently handles SEF control
65	traffic — an RS heartbeat ping, a `SEF_SIGNAL` from PM/RS, a `SEF_INIT` — so the
66	server only sees genuine application messages.
67	
68	The classifier (`server-rt/src/classify.rs`, host-tested) gates each control
69	event on the message's *source*, not its type alone: an RS ping is only honored
70	from RS, a signal only from a signal manager, an init only from RS. A client
71	holding a mere `ipc_to` bit to the server cannot spoof one. `server-rt` is
72	`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` — callbacks travel in the config struct, not global
73	state. The `init_fresh` body most servers use is the shared
74	`sef_publish_to_ds(endpoint, name)` helper, which registers the server in DS.
75	
76	## DS: the name registry
77	
78	Servers discover each other by name through **DS** (`servers/ds/`), a
79	name→endpoint registry backed by a static `[Entry; 16]` table
80	(`servers/ds/src/registry.rs`; the pure `publish` / `retrieve` / `check` helpers
81	are host-tested). A `DS_PUBLISH` request carries a 16-byte NUL-padded name in
82	payload `0..16` and the publisher's endpoint in `16..20`. DS is the one server
83	that *cannot* publish to itself over IPC — a SENDREC to itself before reaching
84	its receive loop would deadlock — so it seeds its own entry in-process during
85	`ds_init`.
86	
87	## SCHED: user-space scheduling
88	
89	The kernel scheduler is **delegatable** rather than replaced. Each `Proc` carries
90	a `scheduler` endpoint; `NONE` (the boot default) means kernel-scheduled — the
91	kernel refills the quantum and rotates the run queue. A non-`NONE` value means the
92	process is scheduled by a user-space server: on quantum exhaustion the kernel
93	dequeues it, leaves `RTS_NO_QUANTUM` set, and sends `SCHEDULING_NO_QUANTUM` to its
94	scheduler, which decides when to re-admit it via `SYS_SCHEDULE`.
95	
96	**SCHED** (`servers/sched/`) is that scheduler. It claims a target with
97	`SYS_SCHEDCTL` (setting `scheduler = SCHED`), tracks it in a static
98	`[SchedProc; 16]` policy table (`servers/sched/src/policy.rs`, host-tested), and
99	on each `SCHEDULING_NO_QUANTUM` refreshes the quantum at a fixed managed band
100	(`USER_Q = 8`, the boot-server band, so a CPU-bound managed process round-robins
101	instead of starving behind kernel-scheduled work). SCHED itself and the kernel
102	tasks stay `NONE` — a scheduler must not schedule itself. `SCHEDULING_START` /
103	`STOP` are the hooks PM drives during fork and exit; MINIX-style priority aging is
104	left for later.
105	
106	## RS: the reincarnation server
107	
108	**RS** (`servers/rs/`) is the system-process monitor and the root of the boot
109	process tree. It arms a periodic one-shot alarm (`SYS_SETALARM`, `ALARM_PERIOD =
110	100` ticks) and on each fire pings a fixed peer set (DS/VM/SCHED/VFS/PM) with
111	`ipc_notify`, tallying acknowledgements in a host-tested monitor
112	(`servers/rs/src/monitor.rs`). Peers acknowledge through the ordinary SEF ping
113	path, so no extra wiring is needed. In Phase 4 restart-on-crash is detect-only —
114	RS counts unresponsive peers but cannot yet re-exec them (exec of a fresh service
115	image is future work). The alarm expiry arrives as a kernel-originated `NOTIFY`
116	from `CLOCK`, which RS distinguishes from its own SEF ping by keying on
117	`m_source == boot_endpoint(CLOCK)`.
118	
119	## PM: the process manager
120	
121	**PM** (`servers/pm/`) owns the POSIX process lifecycle. Its `mproc` table
122	(`servers/pm/src/mproc.rs`, host-tested) records one entry per process — pid,
123	parent, a generation-aware endpoint, and flags. Boot servers and the demo stubs
124	are seeded at init; forked children are allocated from a pool
125	(`[FORK_POOL_BASE, NR_MPROCS)`) where a slot's index is also the child's kernel
126	proc number.
127	
128	User processes drive their whole lifecycle through PM — the POSIX shape, *user →
129	PM, never user → kernel* (the shared user privilege only opens an `ipc_to` edge to
130	PM):
131	
132	- **`PM_GETPID`** replies with the caller's pid (`m_type` *is* the pid, MINIX
133	  result-is-pid), parent pid in the payload.
134	- **`PM_FORK`** builds a child in a fixed, safety-critical order: allocate the

All five review items verified as accurate and fixed. Everything still green: 51/51 markers, 24 VFS host tests, all clippy/fmt/C-ABI gates, stub-free boot.

**1 & 2 — stale `ipc_to = {PM}` claims (nits).** Both real. init's crate doc now says "SENDREC to PM and VFS". For the CLAUDE.md 4.5/4.6/4.8 bullets I **annotated rather than rewrote** — `{PM} as of 4.5 — widened to {PM, VFS} in 5.4` — since those bullets are slice history; rewriting them would erase what each slice actually did. Same treatment for `docs/plans/phase-4-servers.md`. I also found and fixed two more the review didn't list: `book/src/servers/overview.md` still said the user privilege "only opens an `ipc_to` edge to PM", and `book/src/ipc/overview.md` said the same.

**3 & 5 — untested `write_all`, uncovered `len` arms (suggestions).** These share one fix, so I did it once: extracted VFS's pure logic into `servers/vfs/src/write.rs` (`parse` / `validate` / `advance`), the `drivers/tty/src/cdev.rs` split. The payoff is larger than "add some tests":

- **Two of the loop's four rules were untestable by construction** — a driver reporting `0`, and one reporting *more* than it was asked for. Neither is reachable through a working TTY, so in the loop they could only be exercised by breaking the driver. As a step function they're three lines of test each, including a property test sweeping the whole `(off, n)` space to prove the offset never exceeds `len`.
- `len < 0` / `len == 0` now have host tests, including that `len == 0` is checked *before* the buffer — so an empty write never issues a grant, which is the anti-probe property.
- `main.rs` is Sonar-coverage-excluded; a sibling module isn't, so this logic is now measured too.

VFS host tests went 8 → 24.

**4 — bare `UNMAPPED_VA` (suggestion).** Real, with a limit worth naming. The probe only proves what it claims if the address reaches the page-table walk — one that VFS's own `user_range_ok` rejected would answer `EFAULT` a hop earlier and silently test the wrong thing. Added `const _` guards for exactly that: non-NULL, below `USER_VA_TOP`, clear of `USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE`. The two facts it also rests on — init's link base and stack VA — **stay prose**, because neither is a constant a user program can see (`SERVER_STACK_VA` is kernel-internal, the link base is in `user.ld`). I noted that limit in the plan doc rather than implying the guard is complete.

**One judgement call on item 5** you may want to weigh in on: I added a 4th boot probe (`bad-len` → `EINVAL`, marker now `vfs.deny ok n=4`) since an unchecked negative length widens into a ~16 EiB `u64` on the grant — worth an end-to-end marker. I deliberately did **not** add one for `len == 0`: it's a legal no-op, not a denial, and folding it into a battery named `deny` would be a positive assertion wearing the wrong label. Host tests cover it, and the expected-file comment says so.

New mutation run confirms the added probe bites: dropping the negative-length check gives `vfs.deny FAIL bad-len`. Recorded in the plan doc's table (now 8 rows).

Still uncommitted, on `feature/slice-5.4-vfs-write` — 12 files modified, 2 new (`fd.rs`, `write.rs`).

### Update: ./CLAUDE.md — mutation-test workflow

**Why:** This produced a *wrong observation* this session before I caught it. Mutation 2's first form didn't compile; `kernel/build.rs` panicked on the nested server build, the log had zero kernel output, and the checker reported markers MISSING — identical to a successful mutation.

```diff
- ...then `diff -q` each back and `grep -rn MUTATION` to prove nothing leaked into the PR.
+ ...then `diff -q` each back and `grep -rn MUTATION` to prove nothing leaked into the PR.
+ A mutation that fails to **compile** is indistinguishable from one that worked: `kernel/build.rs`
+ panics on the nested server build, the log holds no kernel output at all, and `check-boot-log.sh`
+ reports every marker MISSING. Before recording any observation, `grep -a 'error\[E' <log>` or
+ confirm unrelated markers still PASS (slice 5.4 nearly recorded a false result this way).
```

### Update: ./CLAUDE.md — the `const _` bullet (line 181)

**Why:** Hit while writing the fd table's capacity guard; the fix isn't obvious from the existing text.

```diff
+ A `const _: () = assert!(…)` may not reference a `static` (constants cannot refer to statics) —
+ name the capacity as a `const` first and assert on that, the `vm/region.rs` `MAX_CLIENTS` shape.
```

### Update: ./CLAUDE.md — append to the slice-5.4 bullet

**Why:** The bullet doesn't currently name `write.rs`, and the reason it exists generalizes to every future driver client (BDEV 5.7, MFS 5.8).

```diff
+ Pure logic lives in `servers/vfs/src/write.rs` (`parse`/`validate`/`advance`), the
+ `drivers/tty/src/cdev.rs` split — not just tidiness: **a retry loop's rules for a misbehaving peer
+ are unreachable while the peer works** (a driver reporting `0`, or more than it asked for), so
+ lifting the loop body into a step function is the only way to test them; it also keeps them
+ Sonar-measured, since `main.rs` is coverage-excluded and a sibling module is not.
```

slice 5.4: VFS write path — fd 1/2 → CDEV(TTY)

The POSIX write shape, user → VFS → TTY, with one copy. A user process
hands VFS {fd, buf, len}; VFS resolves the fd to the console minor and
issues a magic grant naming the *caller's* buffer with TTY as grantee, so
TTY safecopies straight out of the caller's address space. VFS never
touches the bytes. First magic-grant consumer on a real data path, and the
rail slice 5.6's musl write()/writev() land on.

ABI: VFS_RQ_BASE = 0x800 with VFS_WRITE {fd 0..4, len 4..8, buf 8..16} —
a raw buffer address, not a grant id, because VFS's client is an ordinary
user process with no grant table. Reply m_type *is* the byte count. The
grant's owner comes from the kernel-stamped m_source and there is
deliberately no payload field for it: VFS holds SYS_PROC, so a
caller-supplied owner would let any client aim a privileged
cross-address-space copy at a third party. PM's and CDEV's band bounds
retarget onto the new neighbour; the C generator gains a 7th band and the
two ordering asserts, but not the payload offsets (deferred to 5.6).

VFS absorbs short writes: CDEV_MAX_IO is a driver staging detail that must
not reach write()'s return, so write_all re-sends with offset advanced
over the same grant. The pure logic — parse/validate/advance — lives in
servers/vfs/src/write.rs (the drivers/tty/src/cdev.rs split), which is
what makes two of the loop's rules testable at all: a driver reporting 0,
or more than it was asked for, are unreachable through a working TTY.

servers/vfs/src/fd.rs is the fd table: fds 0/1/2 pre-opened to the console
in every row, sized from com::NR_SERVED_PROCS. Storage is an immutable
static until slice 5.8's open(), so VFS still carries zero unsafe;
resolve_in takes the rows as a borrowed slice so it survives that switch.

populate_user_priv widens the shared USER slot to ipc_to = {PM, VFS} via
USER_IPC_TO, opening each reverse server → USER reply edge explicitly —
init_boot_image fills a boot server's bitmap only over [0, n_active) and
USER_PRIV_ID is 20.

init is the client and reports through the path under test (user grade, so
no SYS_DIAGCTL and no other way to speak): a banner, a line longer than one
CDEV_WRITE whose returned count it checks, and four denial probes. Four
new boot markers; 51 total, green on both the default and --no-default-
features boots.

Eight mutation tests applied/observed/reverted. Two results differed from
the plan's predictions and are recorded as such: dropping the reverse
VFS → USER ipc_to bit still prints the banner (the request is served; only
the reply is refused) and then hangs init, and dropping the user_range_ok
pre-check moves nothing at all — confirming it is defence in depth and the
kernel's page-table walk is the load-bearing EFAULT gate.

gh pr create --base main --head feature/slice-5.4-vfs-write --title "slice 5.4: VFS write path — fd 1/2 → CDEV(TTY)" --body-file - <<'EOF'
## What

The POSIX write shape — **user → VFS → TTY, with one copy**. A user process hands VFS `{fd, buf, len}`; VFS resolves the fd to the console minor and issues a **magic grant** naming the *caller's* buffer with TTY as grantee, so TTY safecopies straight out of the caller's address space. VFS never touches the bytes.

This is the first magic-grant consumer on a real data path, and the exact rail slice 5.6's musl `write()`/`writev()` wrappers land on (D13).

```
init                VFS                       kernel                TTY
 │ SENDREC VFS_WRITE{fd=1, buf, len}
 ├──────────────────►│
 │                   │ resolve(proc_nr, fd) → CharDev{minor 0}
 │                   │ grant_magic(who_to=TTY, who_from=m_source, buf, len, CPF_READ)
 │                   ├─────────── CDEV_WRITE ──────────────────────►│
 │                   │                    SYS_SAFECOPY(FROM, VFS, gid)
 │                   │            copy_between_as(init → tty staging)
 │◄── reply = total ─┤◄─────────────────────────── reply = bytes ───┤
```

## Design notes

**The grant's owner is the kernel-stamped `m_source`, never a payload field.** VFS holds `SYS_PROC`, which is what makes a magic grant legal for it — so a caller-supplied owner would let *any* VFS client aim a privileged cross-address-space copy at a third party. `VFS_WRITE` has no such field and must never gain one. This is slice 5.2/5.3's confused-deputy rule applied to the *granting* side.

**VFS absorbs short writes.** `CDEV_MAX_IO` is a driver staging detail that must not reach `write()`'s return, so `write_all` re-sends with `offset` advanced over the same grant. An error after partial progress reports the progress (POSIX: those bytes really went out).

**The pure logic is a sibling module** — `servers/vfs/src/write.rs` (`parse`/`validate`/`advance`), the `drivers/tty/src/cdev.rs` split. Not just tidiness: two of the loop's four rules are **unreachable through a working TTY** (a driver reporting `0`, or more than it was asked for), so lifting the loop body into a step function is the only way to test them. It also keeps them Sonar-measured — `main.rs` is coverage-excluded, a sibling module is not.

**The fd table** (`servers/vfs/src/fd.rs`) pre-opens fds 0/1/2 to the console in every row, sized from `com::NR_SERVED_PROCS`. Storage is an **immutable `static`** until slice 5.8's `open`, so VFS still carries zero `unsafe`; `resolve_in` takes the rows as a borrowed slice precisely so it survives that switch untouched.

**Privilege:** `populate_user_priv` widens the shared USER slot to `ipc_to = {PM, VFS}` via `USER_IPC_TO`. Every entry costs a *pair* of bits — `init_boot_image` fills a boot server's bitmap only over `[0, n_active)` and `USER_PRIV_ID` is 20 — so each reverse reply edge is opened explicitly.

## Proof

init is the client and reports **through the path under test**: it holds user grade, so no `SYS_DIAGCTL` and no other way to speak. A regression takes the evidence with it.

Four new markers (51 total), green on both the default and `--no-default-features` boots:

```
minix.rs init: hello via VFS write
vfs-loop-end
minix.rs init: vfs.long ok match=1
minix.rs init: vfs.deny ok n=4
```

`vfs-loop-end` and `vfs.long ok match=1` are independent halves of one contract — a `write()` that moves every byte and replies `OK` prints the tail and is still broken.

## Mutation tests

Eight, each applied / observed / reverted against an uncommitted tree.

| Mutation | Observed |
|---|---|
| Owner from a payload field instead of `m_source` | all four init markers vanish; TTY stays online |
| Drop the short-write loop | `vfs-loop-end` **and** `vfs.long ok match=1` vanish; banner + deny summary survive |
| `resolve_in` accepts any descriptor | `vfs.deny FAIL bad-fd` |
| Drop `ipc_to += VFS` | all four vanish — init's SENDREC refused before VFS sees it |
| Drop the reverse VFS → USER bit | banner **still prints** (request served, only the *reply* refused), then init hangs — 6 markers gone, incl. the fork/exec/exit cycle |
| Reply `OK` instead of the byte count | `vfs.long FAIL` + `vfs.deny FAIL bad-buf` |
| Drop `write::validate`'s negative-length check | `vfs.deny FAIL bad-len` |
| Drop the `user_range_ok` pre-check | **nothing moves** — confirms it is defence in depth, and the kernel's page-table walk is the load-bearing `EFAULT` gate |

Two of these contradicted the plan's predictions and are recorded as such in `docs/plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md`.

## Honest gaps

- The confused-deputy rule is proved **by construction, not by probe** — there is no `who_from` field, so no marker can show a client failing to spoof one. Same shape as 5.2's unprobeable magic-`SYS_PROC` gate.
- Only one process ever writes, so per-process fd rows are exercised at one index at runtime; host tests sweep the whole range instead.

## Verification

- `fmt --check`, `clippy --workspace --all-targets`, `clippy -p minixrs-kernel` (default **and** `--no-default-features`) — all clean
- `cargo test` — 191 pass (kernel-shared 111, gen-c-headers 56, vfs 24)
- C ABI gate: `cargo gen-c-headers` + hermetic `clang -fsyntax-only` — OK, nothing written into the tree
- QEMU: **51/51 markers**, plus the stub-free boot
